catalog.container_strategy: Build from the verified official release archive in an independent directory; install into a resource-local prefix, retain source/license, and use command-local runtime libraries. Keep existing system packages and versions separate.
catalog.purpose: Decode CPU identity, ISA features, caches and raw CPUID records with a C library and command-line tool.
qualification_gaps: Native Linux x86_64 source build and bounded functional checks passed on the recorded host. Exact APT-image deployment and physical target qualification remain separate.
catalog.size_basis: Complete official release archive measured locally and matched to the published SHA-256; logical source bytes sum regular TAR members.

notes: Basic CPU identification needs no root or MSR access. Optional --rdmsr and clock functions are separate hardware operations and are not part of deployment checks.
A container or hypervisor exposes a CPU view. Identification does not establish host frequency, available PMU access, or compiler performance.
The source package includes all upstream CPU identification fixtures. Native verification passed all 501 fixtures for 0.8.2.
The APT cpuid command and libcpuid cpuid_tool are distinct projects and can be selected together.
Each installed ELF tool uses a package-local launcher to load its own shared library. The launcher does not alter the parent environment.
A prebuilt package must record architecture, libc, compiler and build profile. Native build evidence is not an OCI image or arbitrary-platform qualification.
pkg-config metadata uses its containing prefix; legacy libtool .la files retain build-prefix metadata and are not advertised as relocatable link inputs.
